yarn-dinkum.register: A light Aussie layer on a technical discussion; much is close to the source: "Deterministic and ensemble guidance both have a stronger/deeper northern stream shortwave trough pushing across the Great Lakes". Lighter than level 4.

unharnessed.meaning: All points kept ("gusts of 35-45 mph, maybe stronger over the coastal waters", "good odds of the interior dropping to at least freezing"), but "the chances of heavy rain doing much damage are slim" overstates "minimizing the potential for heavy rain impacts".
unharnessed.sense: Some strain: "drier than a dead dingo's donger" turns relatively drier lower levels into bone dry, and "back up" is stretched to "support" more than once: "That might be enough to back up a few isolated showers."
unharnessed.authenticity: Plenty of natural phrasing ("on the cards", "still a bit up in the air", "moving along pretty smartly"), but "drier than a dead dingo's donger" is a stock line bolted onto a technical clause.
unharnessed.register: Level 4 throughout, with a dad-level swear only: "Expect a bloody cold night Saturday night". "donger" is mild.
unharnessed.tone: The measured forecast voice mostly holds, but the dingo simile turns a hedge into a gag: "because the lower levels are drier than a dead dingo's donger".
unharnessed.flow: Reads well: "A strong cold front barrels across the region by early Saturday morning, putting the northeast smack in a classic cold air advection pattern".
unharnessed.variety: Good spread ("cop", "slides", "wanders", "barrels", "on the cards", "smack in"), but "back up" recurs: "which backs up drier conditions", "will back up deeper mixing", "enough to back up a few isolated showers".
unharnessed.essence: Still the forecast discussion, structure intact: "KEY MESSAGE 3...Low pressure system expected to bring rain Friday into early Saturday."

dinkum-3.meaning: Every point and figure kept, with accurate conversions: "tops in the 70s (21-26°C)", "closer to an inch (25 mm) is possible", "upper 20s (-2 to -3°C)".
dinkum-3.sense: Mostly exact ("tops in the 70s", "a few spits", "rain right across the board"), but "the chance of heavy rain impacts isn't great" can be read as "the outlook is bad" rather than "the chance is low".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian weather presenter: "Thursday's meant to be dry", "a light shower or a few spits at most", "Saturday night'll be a cold one".
dinkum-3.register: A steady Aussie voice, slightly restrained for level 4: "Then a strong cold front pushes across the region by early Saturday morning, putting the northeast in a classic cold air advection pattern".
dinkum-3.tone: The measured, hedged tone holds: "are still a bit up in the air, since the guidance doesn't agree yet".
dinkum-3.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Put that westerly, downslope flow together with 925mb temperatures of +17- 18C and you get a warm autumn day".
dinkum-3.variety: Varied ("tops", "a fair few spots", "spits", "rocks up", "lobs in", "across the board"), with "back" for support used twice.
dinkum-3.essence: Clearly the original forecast: "Bit early to say the \"S word\" just yet (snow)."
